main_text.l: VERA METHODUS
INVENIENDI VERUM.
O{nstitueram} ea quæ tribus de
Eruditione libris com-
plexus sum, sine ulla alia anim-
orum præparatione emittere,
contentus sola exhibitione eo-
rum quæ illic continentur,
quippe quæ si rectè animadvertantur, suff-
icere posse videntur ad hoc, ut qui ea ob-
servare voluerint, non eligant falsa pro veris,
non amplexentur umbratilia pro realibus,
verum ad solidam pertingere possint Erudi-
tionem. Sed cum dein animo mecum vol-
verem, quantis quamque adeo multis præ-
judiciis & impedimentis & pravis disposi-
tionibus, iisque non satis penitatis, ne di-
cam parum admodum aut minime detectis,
omnium ferè undique obsessæ essent men-
tes, coepi postmodum, divina fretus ope,
(quæ spes mea est) de Dissertatione aliqua
præliminari concinnanda cogitare, qua com-
prehenderem nonnullas veluti observatio-
nes aut leges, quibus præcipua ex istis ob-
staculis possent removeri, animique dispo-
ni ad faciliorem Librorum sequentium ca-
ptum, praxin & usum. Quod dum exse-
qui contendo, Tractatus integer sub manu
nascitur de vera Methodo inveniendi verum
observatis primis cognitis primisque erratis

marginalia.note: Tractatus hujus ratio, scopus, materia & divisio.

page.notes: The decorated initial is a woodcut C-shaped ornament; the first letter is read as O (printed "Onstitueram"), joined to the word as the initial. The marginal note is printed in small type in three short lines at the right, reproduced here as one note. The printed "Fol. 3" at top right is treated as the page number. The title line ends with a printed dash-like mark after VERUM read as a period. No running head is printed.
